verses.sa: श्री भगवानुवाचअभयं सत्त्वसंशुद्धिः ज्ञानयोगव्यवस्थितिः । दानं दमश्च यज्ञश्च स्वाध्यायस्तप आर्जवम् ॥
verses.tr: Fearlessness, purity of mind, steadfastness in the yoga of knowledge, generosity, self-control, sacrifice, study of the sacred texts, austerity, and straightforwardness.
verses.angle: Fearlessness, abhayanam, as the first step
verses.speaker: Krishna

intro.text: Krishna continues listing the divine qualities, the first of which is the strength to face the world without dread. Listen to how the list begins.

body.text: Fearlessness, purity of mind, steadfastness in the yoga of knowledge, generosity, self-control, sacrifice, study of the sacred texts, austerity, and straightforwardness. Notice how the list begins with abhayanam, fearlessness. After the despair of the battlefield, Krishna names this as the very foundation of a divine life. These divine gifts are followed by qualities like nonviolence, truthfulness, and freedom from anger.

verses.sa: अहिंसा सत्यमक्रोधस्त्यागः शान्तिरपैशुनम् । दया भूतेष्वलोलुप्त्वं मार्दवं ह्रीरचापलम् ॥
verses.tr: Nonviolence, truthfulness, freedom from anger, renunciation, inner calm, absence of slander, compassion for all beings, freedom from greed, gentleness, modesty, and absence of restlessness.
verses.speaker: Krishna

intro.text: Krishna has just named the qualities of a fearless soul. Now he lists the inner habits that make that courage possible. Listen for one quality that protects others from harm.

body.text: Nonviolence, truthfulness, freedom from anger, renunciation, inner calm, absence of slander, compassion for all beings, freedom from greed, gentleness, modesty, and absence of restlessness. Krishna lists ten virtues, and among them is apaisunam, the absence of slander. This quality protects others not through action but through the restraint of speech. Krishna continues with the qualities of splendor, forgiveness, and steadiness that mark a divine nature.

verses.sa: तेजः क्षमा धृतिः शौचमद्रोहो नातिमानिता । भवन्ति सम्पदं दैवीमभिजातस्य भारत ॥
verses.tr: Splendor, forgiveness, steadiness, purity, absence of hostility, and lack of pride belong to the one born with divine qualities, O Bharata.
verses.angle: Naatimanita: the mark of a humble soul
verses.speaker: Krishna

intro.text: Krishna finishes his list of noble traits. Listen for the quality that keeps a person humble.

body.text: Splendor, forgiveness, steadiness, purity, absence of hostility, and lack of pride belong to the one born with divine qualities, O Bharata. Listen to naatimanita, lack of pride. In a list of virtues, this is the quality that stops a person from looking down on anyone else. Next, Krishna names the demonic traits, beginning with hypocrisy and arrogance.

verses.sa: दम्भो दर्पोऽभिमानश्च क्रोधः पारुष्यमेव च । अज्ञानं चाभिजातस्य पार्थ सम्पदमासुरीम् ॥
verses.tr: O son of Pritha, hypocrisy, arrogance, self-importance, anger, harshness, and ignorance are the marks of one born with demonic qualities.
verses.speaker: Krishna

intro.text: Krishna lists six qualities that signal a demonic nature. Keep your ears on the very last word of the list.

body.text: O son of Pritha, hypocrisy, arrogance, self-importance, anger, harshness, and ignorance are the marks of one born with demonic qualities. Hypocrisy, arrogance, conceit, anger, harshness and ignorance mark the demonic nature, Krishna tells Arjuna. Krishna now explains that the divine nature leads to liberation while the demonic leads to bondage.

verses.sa: दैवी सम्पद्विमोक्षाय निबन्धायासुरी मता । मा शुचः सम्पदं दैवीमभिजातोऽसि पाण्डव ॥
verses.tr: The divine nature leads to freedom; the demonic nature leads to bondage. Do not grieve, Pandava. You are born with the divine nature.
verses.angle: Arjuna is born with the divine nature
verses.speaker: Krishna

intro.text: Krishna has just finished describing the demonic traits. Now he turns to Arjuna directly and gives him a single command.

body.text: The divine nature leads to freedom; the demonic nature leads to bondage. Do not grieve, Pandava. You are born with the divine nature. Krishna directly addresses Arjuna as Pandava at the end. The word means born of Pandu, and by using it he reminds Arjuna of his lineage and the divine nature he already carries. Krishna then turns to describe the shadowy qualities that bind a person to the world.

verses.sa: द्वौ भूतसर्गौ लोकेऽस्मिन् दैव आसुर एव च । दैवो विस्तरशः प्रोक्त आसुरं पार्थ मे श्रृणु ॥
verses.tr: In this world there are two kinds of beings: the divine and the shadowed. I have already described the divine in detail; now listen to the shadowed, Arjuna.
verses.angle: Two broad kinds of human nature
verses.speaker: Krishna

intro.text: Krishna has just finished describing the divine qualities. Listen for the second category he now turns to.

body.text: In this world there are two kinds of beings: the divine and the shadowed. I have already described the divine in detail; now listen to the shadowed, Arjuna. Krishna says there are two broad kinds of human nature. He has already spoken in detail about the divine, and now he tells Arjuna to listen to the shadowed, asuric nature. Next, Krishna describes the shadowed nature as lacking purity, truth, and self-control.

verses.sa: प्रवृत्तिं च निवृत्तिं च जना न विदुरासुराः । न शौचं नापि चाचारो न सत्यं तेषु विद्यते ॥
verses.tr: People of a shadowed nature do not know what should be pursued and what should be withdrawn from. In them, there is no purity, no noble conduct, and no truthfulness.
verses.angle: Asuras: unable to tell action from inaction
verses.speaker: Krishna

intro.text: Krishna has just described the divine nature. Now he asks what happens when a person cannot tell right action from wrong withdrawal.

body.text: People of a shadowed nature do not know what should be pursued and what should be withdrawn from. In them, there is no purity, no noble conduct, and no truthfulness. The asuras do not know what to pursue and what to withdraw from, and because they cannot make this basic choice, they end up without purity, conduct, or truth. They say the world is unreal and born only of lust, and they deny any moral order.

verses.tr: They say the world is unreal, without foundation, and without a ruling order, born only from the union of male and female. They say desire alone is its cause, and nothing else.
verses.angle: Untrue world denies a ruling lord
verses.speaker: Krishna

intro.text: Krishna now names the worldview of those with a shadowed nature. Listen to how they explain the world.

body.text: They say the world is unreal, without foundation, and without a ruling order, born only from the union of male and female. They say desire alone is its cause, and nothing else. Listen to the word asatyam, untrue. They call the world untrue and without a ruling lord, denying any higher order. Holding this view, deluded people with ruined discernment and fierce actions arise only to destroy the world.

verses.sa: एतां दृष्टिमवष्टभ्य नष्टात्मानोऽल्पबुद्धयः । प्रभवन्त्युग्रकर्माणः क्षयाय जगतोऽहिताः ॥
verses.tr: Holding this view, deluded people with ruined discernment and fierce actions arise only to destroy the world.
verses.angle: Nastaatmanah: the inner being that is lost
verses.speaker: Krishna

intro.text: Krishna has just described a mindset that denies all order and truth. Now watch for one word that names the inner state of the people who hold it.

body.text: Holding this view, deluded people with ruined discernment and fierce actions arise only to destroy the world. Listen for the word nastaatmanah, those whose inner being is lost. The verse says these people arise for the destruction of the world, and the reason is that they have already lost their true inner self. Next, Krishna describes those who take refuge in desires that can never be filled.

verses.tr: Taking refuge in desires that can never be filled, filled with hypocrisy, pride, and intoxication, they wander under delusion, holding onto impure vows and false beliefs.
verses.speaker: Krishna

intro.text: Krishna turns from false views to the habits that trap a person in delusion. Listen for how he names the inner state.

body.text: Taking refuge in desires that can never be filled, filled with hypocrisy, pride, and intoxication, they wander under delusion, holding onto impure vows and false beliefs. Notice the word asat-grahan, false graspings, and asuchivrata, impure vows. A person living under delusion does not merely hold wrong views; they live by them as their daily conduct. Krishna then shows how these people believe that this world is all there is, with nothing beyond it.

verses.sa: चिन्तामपरिमेयां च प्रलयान्तामुपाश्रिताः । कामोपभोगपरमा एतावदिति निश्िचताः ॥
verses.tr: They take refuge in endless worries that last until death, live only for acquiring and enjoying things, and decide that this is all there is.
verses.angle: Pralayantam: worry as a permanent shelter
verses.speaker: Krishna

intro.text: Carrying on from the previous verse, Krishna now describes the restless inner state of those who live only for desire.

body.text: They take refuge in endless worries that last until death, live only for acquiring and enjoying things, and decide that this is all there is. Here the word pralayantam, lasting until death, shows that their worry is not a passing mood but a permanent shelter. They decide that desire-enjoyment is the highest goal, and that this is all there is. Next Krishna shows how they bind themselves with hundreds of cords of hope to gather wealth unjustly.

verses.tr: Bound by hundreds of cords of hope, driven by desire and anger, they strive to gather wealth unjustly for the enjoyment of desires.
verses.angle: Hundreds of cords of hope bind them
verses.speaker: Krishna

intro.text: Why do people chase wealth so blindly? Krishna points to the trap that binds them, and the engine that pushes them forward.

body.text: Bound by hundreds of cords of hope, driven by desire and anger, they strive to gather wealth unjustly for the enjoyment of desires. The verse names two forces that trap and drive them. Listen for the word baddha, bound, and for the pair kama and krodha, desire and anger, which push them to gather wealth unjustly. Krishna adds that they believe this is everything, and they will fight to keep what they have gained.
